rv.q: The best that can be said about Soul Doctor, a strange Broadway musical based on the life and music of “singing rabbi” Shlomo Carlebach, is that it isn’t as bad as it sounds.
Eric Anderson as Shlomo and Amber Iman as Nina spiritedly lift "Soul Doctor" beyond Old and New Testament realms. Shlomo and Nina's first encounter is worth even the Broadway price of admission.
The show's considerable flaws are more glaringly apparent in this Broadway production performed at the Circle in the Square, newly reconfigured with a proscenium stage.
The new Broadway musical 'Soul Doctor' examines the life and times - and music - of Shlomo Carlebach in a unique, if plodding, study

But it does display a muddy, bumbling, amateurish quality in its storytelling that gets in the way of some fine performances and seriously impedes its ability to grapple with questions as serious as the ones listed above.
I found it disappointing that this intriguing figure came across as a bland, bromide-spouting relic of the hippie era, albeit one tie-dyed in classic Jewish guilt.
While the show did well off-Broadway last summer, its hackneyed awkwardness will spell doom on the main stem.
Unless you’re personally into it, there’s entirely too much of this ponderous religious pedantry to keep an audience alert.
Those intrigued by this passionately performed niche entertainment shouldn’t dawdle.
But a housecall from a show doctor is definitely in order.
But at two and a half hours, this overlong production has far too many that never reach such heights.
Alas, the musical's mix of hokey humor and preachy sentimentality is bound to test the most altruistic spirit.
Too bad they couldn’t have just done a concert of Carlebach’s work intercut with bits of narration instead of this bio musical.
That sort of clumsy, finesse-free storytelling does zip to put the rose in the cheeks of this "Soul Doctor."
A tiresome new bio-musical at Circle in the Square, 'Soul Doctor' does not appear too long for this cruel Broadway world.

vs.sum: Broadway's only thrust-stage theater offers an unmatched intimate experience — no seat is more than a few rows from the action. Sightlines are excellent from every angle, though some seats face actors' backs during certain scenes.

acc.note: Elevator accessible through adjoining building. Loop technology and neck induction systems available.
